title: Do you think the Original Cut of Greed will ever be found?

commenti.body: That would be really cool, but I have to admit the widely available cut (not the 1999 reconstruction) is pretty compelling. I obviously would love a restoration of the original vision. I’m not expecting that to happen, since as the years go on, the film is becoming more and more forgotten unfortunately.

Who knows? But it would be nice. Sadly, if it is somewhere, the odds of it deteriorating to a point of no return increase every day. 

On a side note, I am hoping the Coen brothers get back together and tackle the novel. It's a perfect fit for them. I highly recommend you read if you haven't already.

Nope, it's a pie in the sky fantasy. The script exists, a huge coffee table book loaded with photos exists, and a painstaking reconstruction exists; I'm personally pretty satisfied with these. What we all really need to be clamoring for is a fucking blu ray to purchase of the theatrical release, and also one for the first part of *The Wedding March*. Like, god forbid they even give us a dvd-r as they did for *The Merry Widow* (which Warner Archive release is now something like 13 years old and was quite an excellent edition; the situation is exasperating).

Honestly would way rather have the second part of *The Wedding March* or footage from the missing hour + excised from *Foolish Wives* after its premiere. . . I'm just glad we have what we have from Stroheim, it's the best stuff movies have to offer IMO!

Its sitting somewhere in a vault in South America along with the original cut of The Magnificent Ambersons. 

Adding extra characters for length, Adding extra characters for length, Adding extra characters for length.
Do you honestly think it is sitting in some vault. To me, I feel that is the most likely scenario or it's somewhere in italy.

Ah, I See

though In all honesty, Argentina & Italy are the last 2 places that could have The Original Cut of Greed as those 2 places were the last reported sightings of it as Von Stroheim confirmed that Mussolini had a print of the original cut and reportedly screened the original cut in Argentina.

In fact, his own son, Joseph von Stroheim claimed that when he was in the Army during World War II, he saw a version of the film that took two nights to fully screen, but he could not remember exactly how long it was.

No. Erich von Stroheim was ahead of his time.  What he really wanted to do was a miniseries, like we see on TV each day.  The problem was, back then, the concept simpley didn't exist for serious drama.
